h1:
Kamphaeng Phet with the Family
An Easy 3-Day, 2-Night Plan with Kids
intro: Kamphaeng Phet is easier to do with kids than you'd expect. The town is small, driving is simple, and you get several things kids actually enjoy in one place — a UNESCO old city you can explore by rented bike, a waterfall you can really swim in, and hot springs where you can soak tired feet. We've put together an unhurried 3-day, 2-night plan that leaves room for kids to rest and play.
chips: ♨️ Mineral soak for the whole family

blocks.html: What makes Kamphaeng Phet good for families with kids is that the sights aren't far apart. In-town spots like the Historical Park and the Ping riverside park sit close together, while Khlong Lan Waterfall and Phra Ruang Hot Springs are out-of-town drives you tackle one at a time — so kids aren't stuck in the car all day. This plan lets you start each morning a little later, with time for kids to run around and nap. It isn't a dawn-to-dusk march.

blocks.title: Read before you set off
blocks.html: Nature spots like Khlong Lan Waterfall and the hot springs close around 4:30–5:00 PM, so go from morning to early afternoon and leave time to drive back into town before dark. Some rural roads between districts have little lighting.

items: Day 1 — Old city + the Ping riverside Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park (rent bikes to explore), the Thai-house museum, and a riverside park along the Ping where kids can run around in the evening.
Day 2 — Khlong Lan Waterfall Drive out to swim at the waterfall in Khlong Lan National Park, have lunch by the water, and head back into town in the afternoon.
Day 3 — Phra Ruang Hot Springs A foot soak and a mineral bath to ease tired legs for the whole family before the drive home.

blocks.text: Day 1 — UNESCO old city + the Ping riverside

blocks.html: The first day stays in town all day, with no long drive — good for letting kids settle in after traveling. Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site alongside Sukhothai and Si Satchanalai. The highlight is the Aranyik zone, shaded by large old trees, so biking around doesn't get too hot.

items.activity: Enter Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park, starting at Wat Phra Kaeo and Wat Phra That inside the old city walls.
items.note: Open 8:00 AM–4:30 PM. Entry for Thais is 40 THB adults, 20 THB children. There's a bike rental at the park entrance — older kids can ride on their own, while little ones can sit behind or you can take the tram.

items.activity: Ride on into the Aranyik zone and stop at Wat Chang Rop, where the base of the stupa is ringed by elephant statues. Kids love counting the elephants.
items.note: The Aranyik zone has plenty of shade and is cooler than the in-town area. Bring drinking water and hats.

items.activity: Lunch in town — try the chicken noodles or the egg bananas (kluai khai) the province is known for.
items.note: In-town restaurants are easy to reach and parking is simpler than in the evening.

items.activity: Back to the hotel for the kids to nap, then visit the Kamphaeng Phet National Museum (the Thai-house museum) to see the wooden houses and local way of life.
items.note: The Thai-house buildings are easy to walk through — not so large that kids get worn out.

items.activity: Head to Sirichit Park, a park along the Ping River with a playground and open lawns. Let the kids run around in the cool air.
items.note: Free entry. A nice way to end the day and let the kids burn off energy — the river view is lovely in the evening.

blocks.title: A tip about the bikes
blocks.html: If you're a larger group with young kids, take the tram for a first loop to get the big picture, then rent bikes only for the spots you want to stop and photograph. It's less tiring than pedaling the whole park in one go.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Swimming at Khlong Lan Waterfall

blocks.html: Khlong Lan Waterfall is in Khlong Lan district, about 60–65 km from town — a little over an hour's drive. It's a single big sheet of falling water with a pool at the bottom you can wade into, and the walk from the parking lot to the falls is short. Good for families who don't want a hard trek.

items.activity: Leave town heading for Khlong Lan district. Pack swimwear, towels, and non-slip shoes.
items.note: About an hour's drive. Stop for the restroom and to buy drinking water before entering the park.

items.activity: Enter Khlong Lan National Park and walk about 800 m from the visitor center to the waterfall.
items.note: Entry for Thais is 40 THB adults, 20 THB children, 30 THB per car. Open 8:00 AM–4:30 PM.

items.activity: Swim in the pool below the falls. Keep kids close and pick a shallow spot where the current isn't strong.
items.note: The rocks around the falls are slippery, so keep kids in rubber shoes the whole time and away from any fast-flowing water.

items.activity: Lunch at the park's welfare shop, or spread out a mat for the picnic you've brought.
items.note: There are food stalls and restrooms in the park, but the menu isn't very varied — pack some snacks for the kids just in case.

items.activity: Pack up, walk back to the parking lot, and drive back into town in the afternoon.
items.note: Get back to town before evening so the kids can shower and have a relaxed dinner.

blocks.title: Water levels by season
blocks.html: Khlong Lan Waterfall has water year-round, but late rainy season into early winter is when it's fullest and clearest. In the dry season the water is lower but safer for swimming. If you come during the rainy season, check that the water isn't murky or flowing too hard before letting kids in.

blocks.text: Day 3 — A mineral soak at Phra Ruang Hot Springs

blocks.html: Phra Ruang Hot Springs (Bueng Sap) is in Mueang district, about 22 km from town. It's a natural hot spring that bubbles up at several points, around 40–65°C, with both foot-soak pools and mineral bath rooms. It's a low-key activity to close out the trip before you head home, and a good way to ease the aches from the previous two days.

items.activity: Check out and drive to Phra Ruang Hot Springs, about 30 minutes from town.
items.note: Open 8:00 AM–5:00 PM. Prices are low — a soak or mineral bath runs about ten-odd THB per person, with private bath rooms available to rent.

items.activity: Start at the foot-soak pools. Let the kids try a spot where the water isn't too hot while the adults soak their legs.
items.note: Some spots get very hot — test the temperature with your hand every time, and don't let kids get in on their own.

items.activity: Anyone who wants a full mineral bath can rent a private room — there are both shared and separate rooms.
items.note: Bring your own change of clothes and towels. The area around the pools is shaded with seating to rest.

items.activity: Have lunch nearby, or head back into town to eat before continuing your journey.
items.note: If you're going on to Sukhothai or Nakhon Sawan, this spot sits right along the way.

blocks.html: Staying in Kamphaeng Phet town is the most convenient option — it's near the Historical Park and restaurants, and it's a good base for reaching the waterfall and hot springs in any direction. Pick a hotel with on-site parking and family rooms, which is easiest with kids.

items.name: A hotel in town
items.blurb: Near the Historical Park and restaurants, with easy access to the sights around town — a solid main base for both nights.

items.name: A family-style room
items.blurb: Look for a room with a large bed or an extra bed plus on-site parking, handy when you get back late from the waterfall.

blocks.text: Getting ready to travel Kamphaeng Phet with kids

items: Your own car is easiest — the sights are spread across different districts, and there's little public transport to the waterfall and hot springs.
Pack swimwear + non-slip shoes — useful at both the waterfall and the mineral baths; slippery rocks call for extra care.
Hats, water, sun protection — the old city and waterfall are outdoors, and the sun is strong by mid-morning.
Leave time for the kids to rest — don't cram all three spots into one day; this plan splits a theme per day so kids don't get worn out.
Carry cash — park and hot-spring entry fees are mostly cash only, so bring small bills.

faq.q: Is Kamphaeng Phet doable with young kids?
faq.a: Easily. In-town spots like the Historical Park have trams and bikes to choose from, so there's no long walking, and the riverside park has a playground. At Khlong Lan Waterfall the walk from the parking lot to the falls is short — you just need to keep a close eye on kids while they swim.

faq.q: Can you really swim at Khlong Lan Waterfall, and is it safe for kids?
faq.a: Yes, there's a pool below the falls. Pick a shallow spot where the current isn't strong and keep kids in non-slip shoes the whole time. The rocks around the falls are slippery, so avoid the fast-flowing spots and don't let kids swim unsupervised.

faq.q: Can kids soak at Phra Ruang Hot Springs, and how hot is the water?
faq.a: Phra Ruang Hot Springs runs about 40–65°C depending on the spot. Kids can soak in the foot-soak pools where the water isn't too hot, but always test the temperature with your hand first and keep an adult close. Never let kids get in on their own.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Kamphaeng Phet?
faq.a: With kids and an unhurried pace, 3 days and 2 nights is just right — you get the old city, the waterfall, and the hot springs, one theme per day without cramming. If you're really short on time, 2 days and 1 night covering the old city and the waterfall still makes for a fun trip.

faq.q: When's the best time of year to bring the family to Kamphaeng Phet?
faq.a: Late rainy season into early winter (October–January) is best. Khlong Lan Waterfall is full and clear, and the cooler weather makes it easy to explore the old city all day. In the hot season the waterfall is lower but safer for swimming. Avoid periods of heavy rain, when the falls can flow hard.
